name: Shinjuku
description: Shinjuku, the city that never switches off: Nishi-Shinjuku's towers, the neon of Kabukicho, Golden Gai's tiny bars, the gardens of Shinjuku Gyoen and, in Yotsuya, the shrine stairs of Your Name.

water.note: No sea. The Shibuya River runs in a culvert; the Kanda River's concrete channel in the north-west corner and the ponds of Shinjuku Gyoen and Meiji Jingu are drawn at their own level (inland, pipeline/inland_water.py).

inland.note: The Kanda River about 11 m between concrete revetments 5 m down to a shallow flow (read from photographs, not measured); ponds at the 5 m laser survey's level.

roofs.note: pipeline/arcades.py: Sumitomo Triangle Plaza (r11664668) is a glass atrium closed on every side, not a roof on posts: its glass slopes from low eaves up to the tower (photograph, #258), and the tower's own low solids (r9215167 under 30 m, which PLATEAU files with the tower) are the atrium's other wings; the Opera City Galleria's roof (w787547154, 186 x 13 m at 26 m between the New National Theatre and Opera City) is a glazed roof spanning the walkway, with no posts under it (#258); Keio University Hospital's drop-off canopy (w1409752350) is dark charcoal and flat, its top about one storey up, under the first floor's windows (Niveous Johann's 2022 photograph from the visitors' car park, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0, #323): 5.0 m, its fascia 0.7 m deep

susuki.note: Susuki (trees.json susuki, #326): on the open grassland and meadows OpenStreetMap maps (natural=grassland, landuse=meadow: the unmown grass of the parks and the hills, where susuki is the grass that stands) (Overture base land, OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; pipeline/grasses.py). Its heads stand from mid August to spring (web/trees.js).

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from the cities' street-tree surveys and the parks' own guides: ginkgo and zelkova (keyaki) are Japan's commonest street trees, with plane trees and camphor; the woods are the laurel forest's evergreen broadleaves and camphors, with zelkovas, black pines, maples and a few cedars (sugi, standing for hinoki too). Areas give the parks and precincts known for their own trees a mix of their own; their outlines are OpenStreetMap's (pipeline/tree_areas.py). Somei-yoshino cherries (sakura) line Tokyo's streets after the ginkgo and the zelkova, and stand in the parks' lawns and along the rivers and moats; areas give the places known for them a mix of their own.

areas.name: Kabukicho Central Road
areas.note: Central Road's street trees: slim young trees on a central stem, about 5.5 m, as photographs of 2019 show them (#272)

areas.name: Shinjuku Gyoen
areas.note: The French formal garden's plane avenues, the Japanese garden's pines, the Himalayan cedars (sugi stands in) and camphors. Its cherries are some sixty-five varieties, a thousand trees: the Somei-yoshino and the weeping cherries at the end of March, the double cherries (Kanzan, Ichiyo) through April, and a few kawazu-zakura in February (the garden's guide).

areas.name: Meiji Jingu Gaien
areas.note: The ginkgo avenue to the Seitoku Memorial Picture Gallery, gold in late November.

areas.name: Meiji Jingu
areas.note: The planted shrine forest, now mostly camphor and the evergreen oaks and shii of the laurel forest.

tour.title: Shinjuku
tour.text: The busiest station in the world, three million passengers a day, and around it every Tokyo at once: towers to the west, neon to the east, six-seat bars in Golden Gai and cherry blossom in Shinjuku Gyoen.

tour.title: The stairs of Suga Shrine
tour.text: Stone steps between red handrails, a glimpse of the city below: the stairs where Your Name ends. Fans leave painted ema at the shrine at the top. The film turns ten this year.

tour.title: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building
tour.text: Kenzo Tange's twin-towered city hall, 243 m. Both observation decks at 202 m are free; on a clear winter morning you can see Mount Fuji.

tour.title: Kabukicho after dark
tour.text: Kabukicho Ichibangai's red arch has lit the way in since 1969: neon, karaoke, ramen at 3 a.m., and Godzilla peering over the cinema roof. The district is named for a kabuki theatre that was never built.

protection.title: No sun-access rule for public places
protection.summary: Tokyo protects no park's sunlight. The windows are a lunch-hour thought experiment for this project, as in the Marunouchi model.
protection.source_note: Windows are our own choice (noon to 13:00, all year), not law. The Building Standards Act's shadow rule (日影規制, art. 56-2) limits hours of shadow on neighbouring land in residential-type zones; it does not cover public places and does not apply in commercial districts such as Shinjuku.
protection.reading_note: Tokyo keeps standard time all year.
protection.tip: Tip: try a tower beside Shinjuku Gyoen's west gate.

sources.landmarks: Suga Shrine's 男坂 from the Tokyo stairs database (52 steps, 3.6 m, 16 m, 27°, red iron handrails); its hall, torii and furniture placed from OpenStreetMap and photographs; the Docomo tower's clock (15 m, 150 m up; Tokyo tourism, TV Tokyo) and mast (272 m; SkyscraperPage); Kabukicho's arch (1969; Sanshin Shoji). Signs, screens and shop fronts are indicative.

game.title: Tokyo Pilgrimage: Shinjuku 東京巡礼・新宿
game.blurb: Walk Shinjuku under the real sun: the east exit's screens, Kabukicho's arch, 2-chome's bars, the ginkgo avenue of Jingu Gaien and the stairs of Suga Shrine, ten years after a film made them famous.

lines.title: Report back
lines.on_open: Every walk done. Report back to Nao at the east exit.

quests.title: The east exit
talk: ようこそ新宿へ! I'm Nao. I guide pilgrims: people who come to stand where a story stood. Ten years ago a film put a staircase in Yotsuya on its poster, and games keep sending their heroes into Kabukicho's lanes.

The busiest station in the world is behind you. Look up at the corner: the cat on the curved screen. Across the side street, that white hoarding is where Studio Alta stood from 1980. It closed in February 2025 and came down by this summer.
Then up the street to Kabukicho's red arch, through Ichibangai to the plaza at the top, and say hello to Officer Ono at the koban there. A hand up at the kerb (Y) stops a taxi.

steps.text: Stand under the cat on the corner screen
Look across at the hoarding where Studio Alta stood
Walk under Kabukicho's red arch
Come out on Cine City Plaza
Meet Officer Ono at the Kabukicho koban

quests.title: The stairs
talk: 你好! I flew in from Shanghai for the tenth anniversary. These are the stairs from the poster: Suga Shrine's 男坂.
{landmark:suga.otokozaka.steps} steps, three and a half metres wide, red iron handrails on both sides and down the middle. Count them on the way up.

steps.text: Climb the 男坂
Find Mr Sato by the torii

quests.title: Suga Shrine
talk: Suga Shrine has watched over Yotsuya's eighteen towns since 1634. The hall burned in the 1945 raids; the parishioners rebuilt it.
The great torii went up in 1990. The ema rack is full this year: a lot of them are for the film's tenth.
Read a few. Then, if you like, wait for dusk: the light the film was made of.

choices.text: Show me dusk on the stairs

steps.text: Read an ema on the rack
Stand at the foot of the stairs

quests.title: Shinjuku
talk: Shinjuku 2-chome: a few hundred bars, most of them the size of a living room. A game put a bar here where a journalist drank.
Kabukicho's arch has been red since 1969. See it after dark, then walk up Ichibangai to Officer Ono at the koban by Cine City Plaza.

steps.text: See Kabukicho's arch after dark
Talk to Officer Ono at the koban

quests.title: Kabukicho
talk: Kabukicho is named for a kabuki theatre planned here after the war. It was never built; the name stayed, and the cinemas came instead.

The Koma Theatre stood across the plaza from 1956 to 2008. On its site now, the Toho building: cinemas below, a hotel above, and on the eighth-floor terrace a monster's head, twelve metres of it, fifty-odd metres over the street. Go down Central Road and look up. People call it Godzilla Road now.

The tower behind me opened in 2023: 225 metres, built to look like a fountain springing out of the ground; this plaza had one once. When you've seen the head, find Golden Gai, east past the ward office. Ask for Fumi.

steps.text: Look up at the head over Central Road
Find Fumi where Golden Gai meets the promenade

quests.title: Golden Gai
talk: Golden Gai: six lanes, some two hundred bars, two storeys of wood each, most built in the late fifties. Writers, film people, musicians. Some seat five.

In the bubble years men came with money to buy us out, and some tried worse. Most of us stayed. Now the lanes are full of travellers, and we're glad of them. Read the door before you sit: some bars charge a seat fee.

Hanazono Shrine is just behind us: Shinjuku's own shrine since Edo. In November it holds the rooster fair, Tori-no-ichi, all night, with bamboo rakes for luck. Pay your respects. Then go west, under the great railway bridge, to Omoide Yokocho. Kenta grills there.

steps.text: Walk up to Hanazono Shrine
Find Kenta in Omoide Yokocho, by the west exit

quests.title: Omoide Yokocho
talk: Omoide Yokocho: Memory Lane. It started as a black market by the west exit after the war. Eighty-odd counters now, each under a roof you can touch.

Shinjuku never stops building. Across the road the Odakyu department store's old building came down from 2022; a 48-storey tower, 258 metres, goes up there for the spring of 2030. The lane stays. The smoke stays.
Go and stand at the west exit and watch the cranes. Then come back and eat.

steps.text: Stand at the west exit, under the cranes where the department store stood

quests.title: Aoyama-itchome
talk: This is my stop. In a game a school stood up the road from here. There isn't one; I checked.
What's real: the ginkgo avenue of Meiji Jingu Gaien. 146 trees in four rows, nine metres apart, planted from 1908. They go yellow at the end of November.

steps.text: Walk the ginkgo avenue at Jingu Gaien

quests.title: The Garden of Words
talk: Welcome to Shinjuku Gyoen. I've volunteered in this garden for twelve years.

A film made this Japanese garden famous in 2013: two strangers keep meeting in the shelter by the pond on rainy mornings. The shelter is real, and so is the rain: tsuyu, the rainy season, runs from early June to mid July.

Sit in the shelter and look at the water. Then take the path under the wisteria trellis to the Kyu-Goryotei, the pavilion Taiwan's Japanese residents gave in 1927. The maples go red at the end of November.

choices.text: Wait for the rain in the shelter
I'll walk the garden as it is

steps.text: Sit in the shelter by the pond
Walk under the wisteria trellis
Stand on the Kyu-Goryotei's side of the pond
Meet Kenji on the Shinanomachi footbridge

quests.title: Shinanomachi
talk: You found it. Your Name draws its Tokyo from real streets, and this footbridge outside Shinanomachi Station is one of them.
Look north-west, over the tracks and up the street: the Docomo tower's clock, {landmark:docomo.clock_d_m} metres across.
The film's Tokyo goes on to Yotsuya, one stop east. Haruka studies at Sophia University there; she'll show you the moat.

steps.text: Stand on the footbridge and look up the street
Meet Haruka by Yotsuya Station

quests.title: Yotsuya
talk: Yotsuya Station sits in the old outer moat of Edo Castle. The trains run along the bottom of it; Sophia's sports ground is the drained moat next door.
The film's commuter town is this one: the station, the bank above the tracks, the streets down to Shinanomachi. Walk the bank, then the bridge over the tracks.

Two more, further west. Yoyogi Kaikan stood by Yoyogi Station's west exit, an old block Weathering with You gave a rooftop shrine; it was pulled down from August 2019 and an office building stands there now. And past it, Sangubashi on the Odakyu line, the little station of 5 Centimeters per Second.

steps.text: Walk the moat's bank by Sophia University
Cross over the tracks at Yotsuya Station
Stand where Yoyogi Kaikan stood, by Yoyogi Station's west exit
Find Sangubashi Station on the Odakyu line

quests.title: Pilgrim
talk: お帰り! Stairs, an arch, a bar the size of a living room, a ginkgo avenue. All of it real, and now you've stood in all of it.
Ten years ago a film and a game drew these streets. Now you've walked them. Shibuya's scramble is two stops south on the Yamanote Line, where Aoi guides. Or wait for dusk on the 男坂, or just wander.
